name: Ficus Gabriel Miró II

location.neighbourhood: City centre, the square between the Ayuntamiento and Parque de Canalejas

verified_sources: https://dadesobertes.gva.es/va/dataset/catalogo-de-arboles-monumentales-y-singulares-de-la-comunitat-valenciana (Generalitat Valenciana register, register_id 3035, girth 10.65m, height 25.3m, crown 40.5m)
access: Free, open public plaza in the city centre, no gate or opening hours
transport: TRAM Luceros stop (lines L1-L4), roughly 10 minutes on foot; also served by city bus lines 2, 3, 5, 12 near Federico Soto
verify_notes: One of four large Ficus macrophylla individually registered as 'Ficus Gabriel Miró I-IV' in the Valencian monumental-tree register, all in this one plaza. Local press (todoalicante.es, 2025-09-01) calls this specimen 'the largest ficus catalogued in Spain' with '120 years' and a canopy of 'almost 40m', which matches this register entry's crown of 40.5m closely (the register's own crown figure for II is the largest of the four). Note: a separate older search summary claimed '170 years' for a Gabriel Miró ficus without citing a specific source; treat 120 years (todoalicante, tied to the specific measured canopy) as the better-sourced figure and the 170 figure as unverified. The city has fenced the roots of these trees (alicantepress.com) because visitors climb them for photos, and installed informational plaques (alicante.es) naming this plaza as one of five official ficus-heritage stops. IMPORTANT CONTEXT for the writer: the same plaza also held five old elms (Ulmus minor); one broke and fell at the Gabriel Miró/San Fernando corner in September 2025 (todoalicante.es), which triggered a city-wide review of monumental trees. That elm is NOT this tree and does not affect the ficus, but is worth knowing as recent history of this exact square. No individually dated 'still alive' photo found within this pass; the conservation and signage articles imply active recent stewardship but were not independently dated.

name: Ficus Gabriel Miró IV

location.neighbourhood: City centre, the square between the Ayuntamiento and Parque de Canalejas

access: Free, open public plaza in the city centre, no gate or opening hours
transport: TRAM Luceros stop (lines L1-L4), roughly 10 minutes on foot
verify_notes: Second of the four register-named 'Gabriel Miró' ficus, tallest of the group at 26.6m per the register. El Español (2024-05-11) describes the plaza's ficus collectively as 'probably the most notable specimen[s] of ficus in the entire country' with canopy diameters over 25m, and reports the plaza's current layout dates to 1918 (installation of the 'La Aguadora' sculpture), which the article treats as roughly when these trees would have been planted, consistent with a 100+ year age. No individual age figure found for this specific tree (as opposed to ali_001, which had one tied to it); flagged for that reason. Same plaza context as ali_001 applies (root fencing, informational plaques, the September 2025 elm collapse nearby).

name: Ficus del Passeig de Canalejas

location.address: Passeig/Paseo de Canalejas, Parque de Canalejas, Alicante
location.neighbourhood: City centre, between the Explanada de España and the sports marina

verified_sources: https://dadesobertes.gva.es/va/dataset/catalogo-de-arboles-monumentales-y-singulares-de-la-comunitat-valenciana (register_id 507, girth 11.59m, height 20.8m, crown 38.7m, individually named in the register)
access: Free, public waterfront park (Parque de Canalejas), always open, no gate found
transport: TRAM Luceros stop (lines L1-L4), roughly 12-15 minutes on foot; a few minutes' walk from the Explanada de España and the sports marina
verify_notes: The single largest-girth ficus among this pass's candidates (11.59m, biggest of the shipped set; only the unshipped Ficus de Benalua, held in leads, measures larger at 14.69m). Individually named in the register itself ('Ficus del Passeig de Canalejas'), which is stronger identification than the unnamed Canalejas entries (ali_006/007). Locosporvalencia.com and the older alicantevivo.org piece both independently describe Parque de Canalejas as a public, freely accessible waterfront park designed in 1886 by architect Gonzalez Altes, home to century-old ficus with twisted trunks and aerial roots that have 'accompanied several generations of Alicante residents'. No individual age or planting date found for this specific tree; age fields left empty rather than guessed, per the empty-beats-invented rule. General park age character (elespanol.com) is 'over 100 years' for the macrophylla specimens there.

name: Ficus of Parque de Canalejas

location.neighbourhood: City centre, between the Explanada de España and the sports marina

verified_sources: https://dadesobertes.gva.es/va/dataset/catalogo-de-arboles-monumentales-y-singulares-de-la-comunitat-valenciana (register_id 301, girth 7.05m, height 13m, crown 16m, category Arbol Monumental de Interes Local)
access: Free, public park/plaza area, no gate found
transport: TRAM Luceros stop (lines L1-L4), roughly 10 minutes on foot
verify_notes: One of a tight cluster of four individually registered but UNNAMED Ficus macrophylla (register_ids 300-303) sitting within about 25m of each other, roughly 130-150m from the named 'Gabriel Miro' cluster and inside the same Gabriel Miro/Canalejas green corridor. This is the tallest-girth of the pair shipped from that cluster (7.05m); its sibling 300 (girth 6.43m) and 302 (girth 3.9m) were left in leads to avoid fragmenting one small four-tree grove into four separate collectible points with no individually distinguishing names or stories. El Espanol (2024) states Parque de Canalejas holds 'six ficus macrophylla and 11 ficus nitida', designed 1886; this specimen is consistent with that population but not individually named or dated in any secondary source found, hence flagged. No individual age found; left empty rather than invented.
